evidence.claim: TT simulator fills = imaginary queue position, filled once real volume trades through
evidence.quote: TT models LO executions by assigning orders an imaginary queue position in the LOB, which is filled once sufficient real market volume trades through that position
evidence.source: Lalor and Swishchuk (2024, v3 2026), Market Simulation under Adverse Selection, arXiv:2409.12721

evidence.quote: AFA 3950 / NFA 825 / AFB 3943 / NFB 813; Number of trade order fills that were adverse and non-adverse over 330 simulations throughout the trading on April 24th, 2025.
evidence.source: Lalor and Swishchuk (2024, v3 2026), Market Simulation under Adverse Selection, arXiv:2409.12721

evidence.claim: Ignoring adverse fills and realistic fill probabilities inflates backtests
evidence.quote: excluding adverse fills and realistic non-adverse fill probabilities substantially inflates trading performance
evidence.source: Lalor and Swishchuk (2024, v3 2026), Market Simulation under Adverse Selection, arXiv:2409.12721

evidence.claim: Negative correlation of fill likelihood and post-fill return
evidence.quote: We document a fundamental trade-off: a negative correlation between maker fill likelihood and post-fill returns.
evidence.source: Albers, Cucuringu, Howison, Shestopaloff (2025), The Market Maker's Dilemma, arXiv:2502.18625

evidence.claim: 1-s markout by queue position (Binance BTC perp, ex rebate)
evidence.quote: the average value of -0.058 bp. Conversely, fills from maker orders at the back of the queue predominantly result in negative outcomes ... and an average return of -0.775 bp
evidence.source: Albers, Cucuringu, Howison, Shestopaloff (2025), The Market Maker's Dilemma, arXiv:2502.18625

evidence.claim: Naive maker strategy unprofitable with rebate
evidence.quote: The naive strategy, which is prima facie appealing because it receives the rebate and benefits from the spread, is in fact highly unprofitable.
evidence.source: Albers, Cucuringu, Howison, Shestopaloff (2025), The Market Maker's Dilemma, arXiv:2502.18625

evidence.claim: Fill probability 30% to >90% by queue sizes
evidence.quote: have a low fill probability, as low as 30%. Conversely, the fill probability exceeds 90% when the near-side queue is very small and the opposite-side queue is very large.
evidence.source: Albers, Cucuringu, Howison, Shestopaloff (2025), The Market Maker's Dilemma, arXiv:2502.18625

evidence.claim: Cancellation bias in historical fill probabilities
evidence.quote: given that >95% of submitted maker orders are cancelled ... Lokin and Yu [2024] reports a fill probability of less than 2% for orders placed by other market participants ... compared to the 50% fill probability we find in the same situation
evidence.source: Albers, Cucuringu, Howison, Shestopaloff (2025), The Market Maker's Dilemma, arXiv:2502.18625 (Lokin-Yu secondary-only)
